title: Design a Hotel Booking System
relevance: High — canonical date-range inventory LLD / OOD (campus + SDE-2); Flipkart/Uber/Swiggy-style machine coding and FAANG whiteboards; Hotel Management or Booking.com/Airbnb framing; concurrency + overlap checks are the probe.
company_notes: Campus/machine-coding at Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon new-grad and Indian product cos common as Hotel Management/Booking LLD (overlap correctness over pattern zoo; concurrency as stretch). SDE-2/FAANG-adjacent and Booking.com/Airbnb-style loops expect date-range modeling, TTL holds, payment failure paths, Strategy pricing, and may bridge to HLD. Top-tier LLD alongside Parking Lot, Movie Booking, Library — canonical temporal inventory OOD.

phases.goal: Clarify single-hotel vs platform scope, FRs, NFRs, and stated assumptions before classes.

must_hit.point: Clarify one hotel vs chain/aggregator, book by room number vs RoomType, payment/cancel/housekeeping scope, and whether concurrency + hold TTL are required.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate asks scope questions first: single-property Hotel Management vs multi-hotel booking platform, specific room vs type then assign at check-in, hold TTL, cancel/refund, concurrency.

must_hit.point: Typical single-hotel FRs: manage room types + rooms; search for half-open [checkIn, checkOut); create/cancel reservation; check-in/out; payment; mark maintenance.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists searchAvailable, book/cancel, check-in/check-out, process payment, and admin maintenance as core use cases.

must_hit.point: NFR: no double-booking, thread-safe concurrent holds, extensible pricing/payment, modular services (not one god class).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States correctness (no double-book), concurrency safety, and extensibility of pricing/payment without a god facade.

must_hit.point: State demo assumptions such as one hotel, about 50–200 rooms, hold of 10–15 min, mocked payment, in-memory OK, half-open date ranges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly pins demo knobs: one hotel, ~50–200 rooms, 10–15 min hold, payment mocked, in-memory LLD, half-open ranges.

probes: Is this one hotel’s PMS or a Booking.com-style multi-hotel search-and-book platform?
Is payment and hold TTL in scope for this round?

hints.1: Start by clarifying single property vs aggregator before drawing classes.
hints.2: Separate FR (search/book/cancel/check-in/out/pay) from NFR (no double-book, concurrent holds).
hints.3: Assume one hotel demo, ~50–200 rooms, 10–15 min hold, mocked payment, half-open [checkIn, checkOut) unless told otherwise.

phases.goal: Identify Hotel/Room/RoomType/Guest/Reservation and that inventory lives on a per-room reservation calendar.

must_hit.point: RoomType is category (STANDARD/DELUXE/SUITE + base rate); Room is physical unit with roomNumber — inventory conflicts live on Room, not only on the type enum.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates RoomType enum from concrete Room; says search may be by type but overlap is checked on rooms (or typed pool counts with careful accounting).

must_hit.point: Each Room holds reservations: List<Reservation> as the inventory calendar; isAvailable(checkIn, checkOut) means no overlap with active stays.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts a reservation list/calendar on Room and names isAvailable as overlap over that calendar, not a single BOOKED bit.

must_hit.point: Reservation carries checkIn/checkOut and status PENDING|CONFIRMED|CHECKED_IN|CHECKED_OUT|CANCELLED (plus optional lockedBy/expiresAt for holds).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches Reservation with date range, lifecycle statuses, and hold fields when payment is in scope.

must_hit.point: RoomState (AVAILABLE|OCCUPIED|MAINTENANCE|DIRTY) is for ops, not multi-stay inventory — status alone cannot express booked Mar 13–15 but free Mar 17–22.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out issue #31: flipping Room.status to BOOKED wrongly blocks later non-overlapping stays; ops status vs calendar.

probes: What objects own availability for a date range?
Can Room.status alone model two future non-overlapping stays?

hints.1: Name Hotel, Room, RoomType, Guest, Reservation before patterns.
hints.2: Put the reservation calendar on Room; keep RoomState for occupied/dirty/maintenance.
hints.3: Room.reservations + isAvailable via overlap; RoomType is category only; Reservation status includes PENDING with expiresAt for holds.

phases.goal: Sketch Facade + services and pattern roles without a god class owning inventory alone.

must_hit.point: HotelManagerFacade / HotelManagementSystem orchestrates RoomService, BookingService, PaymentService with searchAvailable / hold / confirm / cancel / checkIn / checkOut.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws a thin facade over room/booking/payment services and names the booking and stay APIs.

must_hit.point: Room owns the overlap invariant (isAvailable/book under lock); BookingService orchestrates hold → price → pay → confirm/release.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Does not scatter the overlap predicate across services; Room checks overlap; BookingService coordinates the two-phase flow.

must_hit.point: Map patterns: State for room/reservation lifecycle, Strategy for pricing and payment, Factory for rooms, optional Observer and amenity Decorator.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names State, PricingStrategy/PaymentStrategy, RoomFactory, and optionally Observer/Decorator without forcing Singleton beyond demos.

must_hit.point: Avoid a god-class facade that also prices, pays, emails, and persists — split SRP or design score drops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps facade thin; pricing/payment/notify live in strategies/services, not one mega-class.

probes: Who owns the overlap check — Room or a random service method?
Which patterns earn points here without turning the facade into a god class?

hints.1: Sketch the facade and three services before coding.
hints.2: Room owns isAvailable; BookingService owns hold/confirm orchestration.
hints.3: Facade + Room calendar + State/Strategy/Factory; Observer/Decorator optional; no Singleton requirement in production.

phases.goal: Implement half-open overlap, search/book/cancel/stay APIs, and optional two-phase hold.

must_hit.point: Ranges [start, end) overlap iff A.start < B.end && B.start < A.end; half-open end so checkout day equals next guest’s check-in day is free.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the overlap predicate and explains same-day checkout/check-in works with half-open intervals.

must_hit.point: searchAvailable(type, checkIn, checkOut) filters rooms with no overlapping active reservations; book/cancel/checkIn/checkOut named on the facade or services.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Implements search against the calendar and names cancel, checkIn (occupy/assign), checkOut (bill + housekeeping/available).

must_hit.point: When payment is in scope: hold room+dates atomically to PENDING + expiresAt, then confirm after pay or release on fail/TTL — never jump AVAILABLE→OCCUPIED while payment is in flight.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes two-phase hold→confirm like movie seats but with date ranges; payment failure releases hold.

must_hit.point: Booked Mar 13–15 still allows Mar 17–20 if date ranges are modeled; status-bit BOOKED would incorrectly block it (issue #31).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks the non-overlapping future-booking example and rejects single-status inventory.

probes: Write the overlap condition for two date ranges.
If someone booked Mar 13–15, can another guest book Mar 17–20?

hints.1: Availability is date-range overlap, not a boolean room flag.
hints.2: Use half-open [checkIn, checkOut) and the A.start < B.end && B.start < A.end test.
hints.3: hold → PENDING+expiresAt → confirm after pay; search scans Room.reservations for non-overlap.

phases.goal: Show how pricing, payment, amenities, and platform stretch plug in without rewriting the critical section.

must_hit.point: PricingStrategy (flat/seasonal/occupancy) and PaymentStrategy (cash/card/UPI) swap without touching the overlap critical section.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places Strategy outside the lock path; BookingService calls strategies after hold or around confirm.

must_hit.point: Decorator layers amenity pricing (breakfast/spa) on base room; Factory creates STANDARD/DELUXE/SUITE rooms.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions amenity Decorator and RoomFactory as in awesome-LLD-style solutions.

must_hit.point: Book RoomType with late assignment at check-in increases occupancy vs booking a specific Room, but needs a pool count/assignment step.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares specific-room booking simplicity vs type-level booking + assign at check-in.

must_hit.point: Platform stretch: searchHotels(city, dates, guests) and hold→pay→confirm across properties; keep full PMS/OTA/ML yield out of scope until asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds multi-hotel search API only as stretch; defers housekeeping schedules, keys, OTAs, yield ML, real PGW.

probes: How would you add seasonal pricing without rewriting book()?
Book by RoomType now and assign a concrete room later — what changes?

hints.1: Pricing and payment should be swappable strategies.
hints.2: Keep Strategy/Decorator outside the per-room lock; Factory for room kinds.
hints.3: PricingStrategy + PaymentStrategy + optional amenity Decorator; type-level book needs pool accounting and check-in assignment.

phases.goal: Prevent double-booking with per-room atomic check+insert, TTL-safe confirm, and strong hold path.

must_hit.point: Two guests racing same room+dates: synchronize per room (or lock inventory rows); check+insert in one critical section; loser gets failure/409.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses synchronized(room) or equivalent per-room lock; no global hotel lock; loser fails cleanly.

must_hit.point: TTL/scheduler releases PENDING holds; confirm conditional on status=PENDING AND locked_by=? AND expires_at > now; must no-op if already CONFIRMED or held by another guest.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Expiry never frees a CONFIRMED stay; unlock only PENDING→available; abandon checkout frees via TTL.

must_hit.point: Search may be slightly stale; hold+confirm must be strongly consistent; multi-instance needs Redis TTL hold plus DB fence (SELECT FOR UPDATE or GiST exclusion) — Redlock alone is not the correctness fence.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits browse vs book consistency; cites DB exclusion/row lock as truth over Redis lock claims.

must_hit.point: Partial multi-room success → all-or-nothing with ordered lock acquisition by roomId; payment retries use idempotency key / conditional confirm on PENDING.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Orders locks to avoid deadlock; confirm is idempotent so double pay retry does not double-create.

probes: Two users book the same room for overlapping dates — what happens?
User never pays — how does inventory free without releasing a confirmed booking?
Would Redis Redlock alone make booking correct across instances?

hints.1: Think check-then-act on one room under a lock.
hints.2: Per-room critical section for overlap check+insert; TTL only for PENDING.
hints.3: Atomic per-room check+insert; conditional confirm; Redis hold + Postgres EXCLUDE USING GIST / FOR UPDATE as final fence — not Redlock alone.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Status-bit (AVAILABLE|BOOKED|OCCUPIED) is simpler but wrong for non-overlapping future stays (issue #31); prefer a reservation calendar + overlap predicate, or per-night inventory rows at platform scale. Ops status stays for occupied/dirty/maintenance only.

One-shot bookRoom is OK for demos; two-phase hold→PENDING+expiresAt→confirm after pay (or release on fail/TTL) matches real booking and is what concurrency follow-ups expect — same pattern as movie seats with date ranges.

tradeoffs.topic: Per-room lock vs DB FOR UPDATE vs GiST exclusion
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Per-room synchronized is the correct LLD demo; use a short DB row lock only to set PENDING+expires_at (do not hold the lock while the user pays); EXCLUDE USING GIST (room_id WITH =, stay WITH &&) is the structural final fence.

tradeoffs.topic: Book specific Room vs book RoomType
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Specific room is simpler for LLD; type-level booking + late assignment at check-in can raise occupancy but needs pool counts and an assignment step — inventory still must not live only on the type enum.
Popular weekends conflict often → pessimistic or conditional insert preferred; OCC alone leads to pay-then-fail unless you still hold first.

gotchas.trap: Using Room.status=BOOKED as the only inventory signal
gotchas.correction: Non-overlapping later stays get blocked; model a date-range calendar per room and check overlap (issue #31).

gotchas.trap: Closed date intervals so same-day checkout and check-in conflict
gotchas.correction: Use half-open [checkIn, checkOut) so checkout day is free for the next check-in.

gotchas.trap: TTL or unlock frees a CONFIRMED reservation or another guest’s hold
gotchas.correction: Release only PENDING held by the same guest; confirm is conditional on PENDING, locked_by, and expires_at > now.

gotchas.trap: Payment retry double-charges or double-creates a booking
gotchas.correction: Idempotency key / reservation id; confirm only while still PENDING.

gotchas.trap: Partial success when booking multiple rooms
gotchas.correction: All-or-nothing transaction; acquire locks ordered by roomId to avoid deadlock.

gotchas.trap: Claiming Redis Redlock alone makes distributed booking correct
gotchas.correction: Use Redis SET NX PX for holds plus DB as source of truth (FOR UPDATE or GiST exclusion); Redlock is not the correctness fence.

gotchas.trap: God-class facade that prices, pays, emails, and persists
gotchas.correction: Keep a thin Facade; split BookingService / PaymentService / Observer notify for SRP.
Physical conflicts live on Room (or typed pool counts with careful accounting), not solely on the type enum.
